'''Kathryn Elizabeth Hare''' (born 1959)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000078994720 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-11-28.</ref> is a Canadian mathematician specializing in [[harmonic analysis]] and [[fractal geometry]].<ref name="profile">{{citation|title=Kathryn E. Hare|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/people-profiles/kathryn-e-hare|work=Pure Mathematics|publisher=University of Waterloo|accessdate=8 December 2017|language=en|date=7 January 2015|archive-date=2016-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305071246/https://uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/people-profiles/kathryn-e-hare|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was the Chair of the [[Pure Mathematics]] Department at the [[University of Waterloo]] from 2014 to 2018.<ref>{{citation|title=Our People: Officers & Administration|work=Pure Mathematics|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/about/people/group/46|publisher=University of Waterloo|accessdate=8 December 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171208233203/https://uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/about/people/group/46|archive-date=2017-12-08|url-status=dead}}</ref>  She retired from the University of Waterloo in 2021.

==Education and career==
Hare did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Waterloo]], graduating in 1981.<ref name="profile"/> She earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of British Columbia]] in 1986. Her dissertation, under the supervision of John J. F. Fournier, was ''Thin Sets and Strict-Two-Associatedness'', and concerned [[group representation]] theory.<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=17617}}</ref>

She was an assistant professor at the [[University of Alberta]] from 1986 to 1988, before she moved back to Waterloo.<ref name="profile"/>

==Awards and recognition==

In 2011, the [[Chalmers University of Technology]] awarded her an Honorary Doctorate for her "prominent research, both in extent and depth, within classical and abstract harmonic analysis".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/news/Pages/Honorary-Doctorates-2011.aspx|title=Honorary Doctorates 2011|date=2011-03-31|website=Chalmers University of Technology|language=en-us|accessdate=2019-06-19}}</ref> In 2020 she was named as a Fellow of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/awards/fellows-of-the-cms/|title=Fellows of the CMS|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|access-date=2021-05-12}}</ref>
